translation: As for what is called thirst from heat of the spleen, the Wei Lun (痿論) says: When the qi of the spleen is hot, then the stomach is dried and one is thirsty, the flesh and muscles become numb, and it develops into flesh wei (肉痿). As for what is called thirst from heat of the kidney, the Ci Re Lun (刺熱論) says: In kidney-heat disease, first there is lumbar pain, soreness of the shanks, bitter thirst with frequent drinking, and body heat. The Re Lun (熱論) says: The shaoyin vessel passes through the kidney, connects with the lung, and is tied to the root of the tongue; therefore the mouth is dry, the tongue parched, and one is thirsty. In recent ages, people only say that kidney deficiency cannot control the heart fire, taking it as upper excess-heat and lower deficiency-cold, and use hot drugs to warmly supplement the kidney water, wishing to make it overcome and expel the heart fire; such people have not understood the way of yin-yang deficiency and excess.
translator_notes: 痿論/刺熱論/熱論 kept as chapter names; 肉痿 rendered 'flesh wei'; 少陰脈 rendered 'shaoyin vessel'.
